answer.label: Not Marilyn Monroe — a modern paraphrase
answer.authorDates: Wording undocumented before the 2000s · falsely credited to Marilyn Monroe
answer.sourceLine: This body-positivity slogan appears in no interview, letter, or documented statement by Marilyn Monroe, and it is listed among her misattributed quotes on Wikiquote ↗. The wording is anachronistic: the standardized clothing term “size zero” was not part of the vocabulary of Monroe’s lifetime (she died in 1962), and no primary source ties this exact line to her.

source.heading: The quote in question
source.excerpt: To all the girls that think you're fat because you're not a size zero, you're the beautiful one. It's society who's ugly.
trail: Wikiquote catalogues this line in the Misattributed section of its Marilyn Monroe page ↗, with no source given.
The long-running fan archive alwaysmarilynmonroe flags it as fake ↗, noting the standardized term “size zero” postdates Monroe’s lifetime.
It spreads through aggregators such as Goodreads ↗ and Quotefancy ↗, always undated and without citation.
source.excerptNote: No interview, letter, or documented statement by Marilyn Monroe contains this line; it circulates only as an undated, unsourced slogan.
source.rightsNote: The exact wording has no identifiable author or first-publication source — it reads as an anonymous modern slogan misattributed to Marilyn Monroe. With no work or date to tie it to, no copyright status can be responsibly asserted.

author.name: Marilyn Monroe
author.heading: The name attached to the quote
author.bio: Marilyn Monroe (born Norma Jeane Mortenson) was one of Hollywood’s most enduring stars, famous for films such as Some Like It Hot and Gentlemen Prefer Blondes. Because her image is a magnet for feel-good and empowerment slogans, she is among the internet’s most heavily misquoted figures — her documented interviews and writings (collected in Fragments, 2010) contain nothing resembling this line.

misattribution.heading: The misattribution
misattribution.intro: This is a modern body-positivity slogan pinned onto Marilyn Monroe — one of the internet’s most common vehicles for feel-good quotes with no origin. Nothing in her documented record contains it.

items.why: The line appears in none of Monroe’s interviews, letters, or writings and is catalogued under Misattributed on Wikiquote ↗, with no source ever supplied.
The standardized clothing term “size zero” belongs to a later era of vanity sizing, not the vocabulary of Monroe’s lifetime — a point flagged by the alwaysmarilynmonroe archive ↗. She died in 1962.

misattribution.truthLine: The honest answer: Marilyn Monroe never said this. It is an anonymous modern slogan misattributed to her, and it is listed as misattributed on Wikiquote ↗.

context.heading: Why it spread
lead: Marilyn Monroe has become a lightning rod for empowerment and body-positivity slogans she never uttered. Her genuine, documented reflections were collected in Fragments (2010); this line is not among them, nor in any interview or letter.

The tell is in the language itself. “Size zero” as a standardized clothing designation belongs to a later era of fashion sizing, not to the 1950s. The slogan’s sentiment is a 21st-century one, retro-fitted onto a mid-century icon to lend it authority.
context.pull: Marilyn died in 1962 — long before “size zero” entered the fashion lexicon.
